title: Sampling variability, noise, and other annoyances

cues.en: Mike: Variability is one of the most important concepts in statistics and probability.
cues.zh: Mike：變異是統計與機率中最重要的概念之一。

cues.en: It's also one of the biggest sources of annoyances in scientific research.
cues.zh: 也是科學研究最令人煩惱的來源之一。

cues.en: So I thought I'd have this video to explain a little bit more about sampling variability, make sure that we all are on the same page about what sampling variability means,
cues.zh: 所以想透過這部影片，進一步解釋抽樣變異，確保大家對這個詞有相同理解，

cues.en: and discuss a few points of where variability comes from and why it's important to understand these different sources of variability.
cues.zh: 並討論變異來自哪裡，以及為什麼了解不同來源很重要。

cues.en: Okay, so let's start with our scientific question.
cues.zh: 先從科學問題開始。

cues.en: You can see these are the kinds of questions that I'm often puzzled by.
cues.zh: 可以看到，這就是經常困擾我的問題類型。

cues.en: How tall is the average Montenegrin?
cues.zh: 蒙特內哥羅人的平均身高是多少？

cues.en: What is a Montenegrin?
cues.zh: 什麼是蒙特內哥羅人？

cues.en: Is that some weird animal that lives on the plains of Africa?
cues.zh: 是生活在非洲平原的某種奇怪動物嗎？

cues.en: No, no, no.
cues.zh: 不，不，不。

cues.en: And Montenegrin is a person who lives in a country called Montenegro.
cues.zh: 蒙特內哥羅人，就是住在蒙特內哥羅這個國家的人。

cues.en: I've never been to this country, but I've seen pictures of it.
cues.zh: 我沒去過，但看過照片。

cues.en: It looks really beautiful.
cues.zh: 看起來非常美。

cues.en: I would like to go visit there someday.
cues.zh: 希望有一天能去看看。

cues.en: Okay, but, so let's say, you know, we take a trip, a scientific journey to Montenegro.
cues.zh: 好，假設我們去一趟蒙特內哥羅，進行科學之旅。

cues.en: We want to know how tall is the average Montenegrin.
cues.zh: 想知道蒙特內哥羅人的平均身高。

cues.en: Now, actually, for right now, I don't care about the actual answer.
cues.zh: 目前其實不在意實際答案。

cues.en: It doesn't really matter for the purposes of this lecture.
cues.zh: 就這堂課而言，沒有關係。

cues.en: It doesn't matter what the actual answer is.
cues.zh: 實際答案是什麼，並不重要。

cues.en: The question is, how do we know the answer?
cues.zh: 問題是，如何知道答案？

cues.en: How do we go about finding the answer?
cues.zh: 該怎麼找出答案？

cues.en: Well, I guess you're probably thinking that you just stay at home and Google it, look it up on the internet.
cues.zh: 我猜你可能會想，待在家裡用 Google 搜尋，上網查就好。

cues.en: But someone somewhere had to know this answer.
cues.zh: 但總得有人在某處知道這個答案。

cues.en: Someone had to go out and find this answer by measuring Montenegrins.
cues.zh: 總得有人出去測量蒙特內哥羅人，找出答案。

cues.en: So let's imagine we have our population of Montenegrins, which is actually way, way, way, way, way bigger than this.
cues.zh: 假設這是蒙特內哥羅人的母體，實際上當然比這大得多得多。

cues.en: It's just a picture of a lot of people.
cues.zh: 這只是一張很多人的照片。

cues.en: So what we do is we say, well, you know, I'm just gonna pick one person.
cues.zh: 我們可能會說，只挑一個人。

cues.en: I'll fly to Montenegro, and as soon as I get off the airplane, the first person I meet, I'm going to measure how tall they are.
cues.zh: 飛到蒙特內哥羅，一下飛機，遇到第一個人就量身高。

cues.en: So pick this person here, and random person 1 has a height of 160 centimeters.
cues.zh: 選這個人，隨機的第一個人身高是 160 公分。

cues.en: So I say, okay, fine, we know the height of the average Montenegrin, but you know that that's not necessarily going to be the height of the average Montenegrin.
cues.zh: 於是說，好，知道平均身高了。但你知道，這不一定就是蒙特內哥羅人的平均身高。

cues.en: So, okay, we walk into town a bit and we measure someone else.
cues.zh: 所以再往市區走一點，測量另一個人。

cues.en: So we stop someone else.
cues.zh: 攔下另一個人。

cues.en: And this person and Uhoh, this person is considerably taller so they don't have the same height.
cues.zh: 這個人，喔，明顯高得多，所以身高不同。

cues.en: So we continue this and measure from a lot of other individuals, and we see that there's quite some variability.
cues.zh: 繼續測量更多個人，就會看到相當大的變異。

cues.en: So not every person has exactly the same height, but you know, I looked up on the internet and the internet said that the average Montenegrin is 183.2 centimeters,
cues.zh: 不是每個人身高都完全相同，但我上網查過，網路說蒙特內哥羅人的平均身高是 183.2 公分，

cues.en: and this has to be true because I saw it somewhere on the internet.
cues.zh: 這一定是真的，因為我在網路某個地方看到了。

cues.en: So how do we reconcile the fact that if, you know, the true population average height is 138.2 centimeters,
cues.zh: 所以，如果真正母體平均身高是 138.2 公分，

cues.en: how can we have people who have different heights than what the population average is?
cues.zh: 為什麼還有人和母體平均值不同？該怎麼解釋？

cues.en: Well, obviously, you know the answer, it's just due to variability.
cues.zh: 顯然，你知道答案，只是因為變異。

cues.en: Not everyone is going to have exactly the same height.
cues.zh: 不是每個人都會有完全相同的身高。

cues.en: So this is sampling variability.
cues.zh: 這就是抽樣變異。

cues.en: Different samples from the same population can have different values of the same measurement.
cues.zh: 同一個母體中的不同樣本，對相同量測可能有不同數值。

cues.en: So same measurement, same population, but different samples can have different values.
cues.zh: 相同量測、相同母體，但不同樣本可能有不同值。

cues.en: That's what sampling variability means.
cues.zh: 這就是抽樣變異的意思。

cues.en: And the implication of sampling variability is that one single measurement is likely to be an unreliable estimate of a population parameter.
cues.zh: 其含意是，單一量測很可能不是可靠的母體參數估計。

cues.en: Now, how unreliable that estimate is depends on a variety of factors.
cues.zh: 至於多不可靠，取決於許多因素。

cues.en: It depends on where the variability comes from, why there is that variability in the first place and so on.
cues.zh: 取決於變異來自哪裡、為什麼存在這些變異等等。

cues.en: So I hope this is all rather intuitive, but I think it's important to lay it out and make sure that we are all on the same page with the terminology.
cues.zh: 希望這些都相當直觀，但我認為有必要清楚說明，確保大家對術語理解一致。

cues.en: So same population, same measurement, but different samples can give different values.
cues.zh: 相同母體、相同量測，但不同樣本可能給出不同數值。

cues.en: That is the definition of sampling variability.
cues.zh: 這就是抽樣變異的定義。

cues.en: So where does sampling variability come from?
cues.zh: 那抽樣變異從哪裡來？

cues.en: Well, there is natural variation, which is often seen in biology.
cues.zh: 有自然變異，生物學中經常可見。

cues.en: All sorts of biological parameters have natural variability.
cues.zh: 各種生物參數都有自然變異。

cues.en: And also in physics, there's a lot of natural variation like earthquake magnitudes and the number of stars per galaxy and so on.
cues.zh: 物理中也有很多，例如地震規模、每個星系的恆星數量等等。

cues.en: Of course, there are other areas of physics where there is very little variability, like the size of a proton, for example.
cues.zh: 當然，物理某些領域的變異很小，例如質子的大小。

cues.en: There isn't really appreciable differences in different atoms in the size of an individual proton.
cues.zh: 不同原子中，個別質子的大小並沒有可察覺的差異。

cues.en: So sometimes there's more variability, sometimes there's less variability.
cues.zh: 所以有時變異多，有時少。

cues.en: It also depends on measurement noise.
cues.zh: 也取決於量測雜訊。

cues.en: So maybe your sensors are imperfect, maybe you have some problems with your sensors.
cues.zh: 也許感測器不完美，或者有一些問題。

cues.en: Maybe the sensors are noisy, or maybe they're just not that precise.
cues.zh: 也許有雜訊，或者只是精密度不夠。

cues.en: Imagine you have a scale, a weight scale that has a precision of grams, but you're trying to measure something that's in the range of micrograms.
cues.zh: 想像有一台精度到公克的秤，但想測量微克範圍的東西。

cues.en: So now the sensors may be, you know, decent enough, but they're not precise enough to measure the phenomenon that you are trying to measure with a sufficient exactness.
cues.zh: 感測器也許本身不錯，但精密度不足以用足夠的精確程度，量測你想測的現象。

cues.en: So there's natural variation, there's measurement noise, and complex systems have a lot of factors that influence the outcome variable.
cues.zh: 所以有自然變異、量測雜訊，而複雜系統還有很多會影響結果變數的因素。

cues.en: So we can go back to height as a really simple example.
cues.zh: 可以回到身高這個簡單例子。

cues.en: If we would ignore height and just measure the age of a bunch of randomly selected people ignoring, sorry, measure the height of randomly selected people ignoring age,
cues.zh: 如果忽略身高，只測量一群隨機選取者的年齡，抱歉，是隨機測身高而忽略年齡，

cues.en: then obviously, there would be much, much, much bigger variability and you would know immediately that that's not a fair thing to do.
cues.zh: 顯然變異就會大得多，而且你會立刻知道，這樣做並不公平。

cues.en: Of course, even when I'm keeping age constant, that doesn't guarantee that we are going to get the same heights across different individuals.
cues.zh: 當然，即使讓年齡保持一致，也不保證不同人的身高相同。

cues.en: But if you keep the age fixed, that's certainly going to reduce the variability in height compared to ignoring age and pooling together a bunch of babies
cues.zh: 但固定年齡，相較於忽略年齡，把一群嬰兒

cues.en: and a bunch of full grown adults and measuring all of their heights.
cues.zh: 和一群成年人的身高混在一起測量，肯定能降低身高變異。

cues.en: Okay, so these are some sources of sampling variability.
cues.zh: 好，這是抽樣變異的一些來源。

cues.en: Some of these sources you can control in your experiments, so a well-designed experiments should have sufficiently good sensors
cues.zh: 有些來源可以在實驗中控制，例如設計良好的實驗，應該有足夠好的感測器，

cues.en: that there isn't a whole lot of measurement noise.
cues.zh: 不至於產生太多量測雜訊。

cues.en: And you, as the scientist, you, as the researcher, should be thinking about some of these factors that you need to control for or to hold constant.
cues.zh: 身為科學家、研究者，也應該思考哪些因素需要控制，或維持固定。

cues.en: And some sources of variability are just not possible to control.
cues.zh: 而有些變異來源根本無法控制。

cues.en: And maybe we don't want to control them because maybe it's important to know that some factors in biology are variable and inherently variable across individuals.
cues.zh: 也許也不想控制，因為知道某些生物因素在不同個體間，本質上就有變異，可能很重要。

cues.en: And the last source that I list here is just some intrinsic stochasticness that the universe is a wild, unpredictable, and random place.
cues.zh: 最後列出的來源，是某種內在隨機性：宇宙是個狂野、不可預測、隨機的地方。

cues.en: And so there just is variability that, you know, it's just literally impossible to quantify or predict, or at least, is well outside of our current knowledge.
cues.zh: 因此有些變異真的不可能量化或預測，至少遠遠超出目前的知識。

cues.en: Okay, so what to do about sampling variability?
cues.zh: 那如何處理抽樣變異？

cues.en: Well, you already know part of the answer and that is take many samples.
cues.zh: 你已經知道部分答案，就是取得很多樣本。

cues.en: So we would never trust the average height of a population based on measuring one individual person.
cues.zh: 不會只測一個人，就相信能得到母體平均身高。

cues.en: So what we do is we measure a bunch of people, we measure a lot of people, and we average together.
cues.zh: 所以測量一群人、很多人，再取平均。

cues.en: And here, there's a key underlying assumption, which is that the variability is both positive and negative, which is to say that the,
cues.zh: 這裡有個關鍵假設，就是變異同時有正有負，也就是說，

cues.en: when you're looking at average height, for example, that there's variability both above the average height and below the average height.
cues.zh: 例如觀察平均身高時，平均值上方和下方都有變異。

cues.en: So by averaging together, then we get a convergence to the true population mean.
cues.zh: 所以把它們平均，就會收斂到真正母體平均值。

cues.en: I'm gonna talk more about this idea, why this works.
cues.zh: 之後會進一步談這個概念，解釋為什麼有效。

cues.en: You know, you have an intuition that averaging together more samples is a good idea.
cues.zh: 直覺上，你知道把更多樣本平均是好主意。

cues.en: And the reason why it works has to do with something called the law of large numbers.
cues.zh: 原因和所謂的大數法則有關。

cues.en: And there's a whole video about this concept in a few videos from now.
cues.zh: 再過幾部影片，會有一整部介紹這個概念。

cues.en: And another thing you can do about sampling variability is to run statistical analyses.
cues.zh: 另一種處理抽樣變異的方式，是進行統計分析。

cues.en: For example, you can compute confidence intervals around your parameter estimates, around your sample means and your sample variances and so on.
cues.zh: 例如，在參數估計值、樣本平均值、樣本變異數等等周圍計算信賴區間。

cues.en: Those confidence intervals will tell you about the relationship between the parameter estimates and the true parameter values in the population.
cues.zh: 那些信賴區間會告訴你，參數估計和母體真實參數值的關係。

cues.en: All right, so in this video, I talked about sampling variability.
cues.zh: 這部影片討論了抽樣變異。

cues.en: I talked about some of the sources of where sampling variability comes from and why it's important to understand sampling variability.
cues.zh: 介紹它的一些來源，以及為什麼了解抽樣變異很重要。
